title: [divergent][R-19-022] ux_led Zephyr backend: 16ms evaluation tick is a permanent periodic heartbeat
description: spec/19-device-ux.md §6/§2: 'LED changes are events, not heartbeats' and tier-H truth is ~0 power cost; a design requiring periodic work to feel alive is wrong at this layer. Evidence: lichen/subsys/lichen/ux/ux_led_zephyr.c:25,36-42 — UX_LED_TICK_MS=16 with unconditional k_work_reschedule in ux_led_tick(): the system workqueue wakes 62.5x/sec forever to re-evaluate the on/off verdict, even when the LED state is steady (joined-idle off included). State transitions themselves are event-driven (lichen_ux_led_state_set), but pattern *rendering* is a permanent heartbeat with real battery cost on a mesh node. Upgrade path: compute the next pattern edge (on→off / off→on from the current state's period/on_ms) and schedule the tick at that deadline instead of a fixed 16ms; steady states (joined-idle off) schedule nothing. The no-LED no-op path already does exactly this correctly (ux_led_zephyr.c:49-53) — extend the same discipline to the with-LED case. Host engine (ux_led_core.c eval) is unaffected; only the backend tick policy changes.
